title: Filtering Technology for Three-Level Converters with Series-Connected Power Devices
content: A study of the filtering technology for a 10 MW medium-voltage Active Neutral-Point-Clamped (ANPC) three-level converter employing series-connected Integrated Gate-Commutated Thyristor (IGCT) devices is presented. The ANPC three-level topology with series-connected IGCTs and its four commutation paths are first introduced. A passive damping improvement scheme is then proposed, in which an LC network is connected in parallel with the damping resistor of the LCL filter. By exploiting the frequency-selective current-sharing characteristics—the capacitor passing high-frequency currents and the inductor passing low-frequency currents—the damping resistor power loss is reduced from 6.4 kW to 462 W, representing a 93% reduction. Furthermore, a notch-filter-based active damping scheme, discretized via the Tustin transformation and embedded in the current control loop, is introduced to achieve precise suppression of the LCL resonance peak. In addition, a DPWM1 strategy based on hybrid fundamental-frequency modulation is proposed, which raises the effective switching frequency from 750 Hz to 1050 Hz, thereby creating favorable conditions for setting the filter resonance frequency. Simulation results demonstrate that under rated operating conditions and within a ±30% reactive power regulation range, the grid-injected current total harmonic distortion (THD) satisfies the IEEE Std 519-2022 (THD <5%), and the 11th-order harmonic content meets the <2% limit.
